summary: Intermittent canary handshake skipped for pinned tenant after client keepalive reconnects
description: Customer BrightDocs reports occasional loss of pinned model affinity during canary windows. Symptoms: requests from a pinned tenant are routed to fallback canary variant instead of the pinned model after the client's TCP connection is reset by keepalive. Issue appears only during staged canary windows and correlates with frequent short-lived connections from the client's SDK.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs traffic to pinned model redwood-chat-v1.3 in us-east-1 (dedicated pool).
2) Issue reproducer: create client that issues many short RPCs and enforces aggressive TCP keepalive (interval 10s, timeout 5s), causing socket reconnects between requests.
3) Trigger a canary weight change (e.g., shift 5% -> 20%) or a small prewarm oncohort update.
4) Observe some requests from the tenant routed to the canary/degraded variant instead of the pinned model, despite explicit pin set in tenant configuration.
logs: edge-proxy: [2025-11-02T18:12:03Z] INFO request start tenant=brightdocs session=abc123 conn=10.0.5.12:3456
edge-proxy: [2025-11-02T18:12:04Z] WARN connection reset by peer, conn=10.0.5.12:3456
orchestrator: [2025-11-02T18:12:04Z] DEBUG handshake skipped: missing-session-header tenant=brightdocs session=abc123
router: [2025-11-02T18:12:04Z] INFO route selected fallback-variant="degraded-v1" for tenant=brightdocs (pin present but handshake state absent)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: aggressive keepalive triggers connection teardown before the edge can commit the session handshake; new connection resumes without the ephemeral session header, orchestrator treats request as not pinned and applies fallback routing.
Confirmed via logs: a small percentage (~0.3%) of requests in the customer's traffic trace show 'handshake skipped: missing-session-header' immediately after TCP keepalive resets.

Edge-proxy code path: session header is populated from an in-memory connection-bound store. When connections are short-lived, header population sometimes occurs after client reconnect, creating a race between header initialization and first request on new socket.
Reproducer built with local client shows deterministic failure when keepalive interval <= 10s and request rate < 1 r/s per connection.

Related to known issue SUP-999999 where prewarm mirror and session initialization order caused ephemeral pin loss; however this reproducer is specific to connection lifecycle rather than prewarm ordering.

Data from observability: tenant token affinity metric dropped for 7s windows aligning with reconnect bursts. No errors from serving-runtime; fallback routing caused quality delta for affected calls only.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) [2025-11-02]: Customer reported 12 incidents over last 48 hours where pinned responses came from degraded variant. Attached SDK trace and pcap. Asked for initial triage.
Ethan Walters (SRE) [2025-11-02]: Reproduced locally with aggressive keepalive. Observed handshake-skip logs. Opening edge-proxy PR to guard header population on accept path (see related PR).

SRE on-call (2025-11-03): Rolled temporary mitigation: fall back to consult tenant pin via control-plane cache when handshake header is absent and pin TTL is recent (heuristic). This reduced customer incidents to near-zero in the canary window but is not a full fix.
Customer BrightDocs (Support) [2025-11-04]: Confirmed mitigations decreased occurrence. Asked for timeline for permanent fix as they can't change SDK keepalive globally.

Engineering (Edge) [2025-11-05]: Proposed fix: ensure session-header init happens synchronously in accept handshake, and add defensive lookup of tenant-pin from local LRU cache when header missing. Preparing patch + unit tests. Target deploy to staging 2025-11-08.
next_steps: 1) Land edge-proxy PR to initialize session header on accept and add defensive control-plane cache fallback (PR referenced above).
2) Deploy to staging and run customer reproducer for keepalive flows.
3) If staging looks good, schedule a canary deploy to prod-us-east-1 during low-traffic window and monitor tenant affinity metrics and fallback rate.
4) Post-deploy, follow up with BrightDocs with timeline and recommend SDK keepalive tuning as long-term best practice.
5) Create an internal doc describing the connection lifecycle and pin handshake ordering to prevent recurrence.
